fidelity.detail: PySub objects (str, list, dict) are heap-allocated by the runtime and CPython reclaims them by reference counting.
fidelity.mitigation: library wrappers run each call inside a memory arena that frees every str/list/dict allocated during the call after the result has been copied back; nothing leaks across calls.

fidelity.cls: L1 copy semantics at the Python boundary
fidelity.detail: Arguments are copied into the compiled runtime and results copied back, so object identity, aliasing between arguments (the same list passed twice) and tuples are not preserved.
fidelity.mitigation: list/dict arguments the function may mutate are written back into the caller's object in place after the call (also when an exception is raised).
